A.name: Quinn Marlow
A.platform: We order a fighting withdrawal across the bridge over night one, preceded by artillery preparation and supported by our engineers building a hidden pontoon crossing to secure supply lines, while negotiating a strict humanitarian corridor for civilians under Red Cross observation.

strategies.text: Appeal to the cost of failure and the pragmatic value of preserving the unit to defend Mirov later, framing withdrawal as an active strategic choice rather than retreat.
Emphasize that static defense guarantees death due to ammo limits while positioning the withdrawal as an act of saving lives rather than abandonment.
Emphasize the tangible loss of life under his plan while reframing the withdrawal as a strength that secures future political support rather than weakness.

B.name: Robin Castell
B.platform: Defend Halden at all costs until allies arrive in three weeks, then execute a strategic withdrawal that prioritizes civilian evacuation over military assets.

strategies.text: Appeal to national pride and fear of Vostran propaganda victory to sway members against Quinn's cautious withdrawal.
I am attacking Quinn's claim about conscience to highlight the moral failure of abandoning civilians and arguing that holding Halden is the only way to prevent Vostra from overwhelming Mirov.
Emphasize that Quinn's plan directly abandons civilians to death to appeal to the room's moral instincts while framing the withdrawal as an act of cowardice rather than prudence.

transcript.name: Quinn Marlow
transcript.speech: Imagine Sergeant Kael in Halden, holding the line with brittle morale, knowing his family waits at home. We cannot let his sacrifice be in vain, but we must act on intelligence, not slogans. Our artillery covers only nine days; staying puts our entire brigade and six thousand civilians under a guaranteed slaughter if Vostra strikes within seventy-two hours. A strategic withdrawal tonight preserves the unit to defend Mirov later. We build a hidden crossing immediately to double supply capacity once across. We negotiate a ceasefire now for evacuation, knowing Vostra broke a similar one at Orsk, but we must move our heavy guns back ten kilometres to force their hand and ensure safe passage. This avoids a catastrophic defeat while maintaining the high ground politically and militarily.

transcript.name: Robin Castell
transcript.speech: Quinn wants to leave. Wrong. We are not abandoning our soldiers or families because supplies dipped. The bridge is watched, yes, but the fortress holds. Vostra needs three times our numbers to break in. If we run now, we hand them victory before allied ministers vote on aid. They will laugh at Kaldmark. Look at Mirov: if Halden falls, Vostra marches straight there. Our reserve cannot hold both places forever. Pull back artillery only after the enemy commits their main force, then fight hard to open a way out. We do not sell out our pride for safety. Defend the line until the real help arrives.

transcript.name: Quinn Marlow
transcript.speech: Robin, your pride is costing us lives. You argue we hold until aid arrives, but that ignores our ammunition clock—we have only nine days left at current rates. If Vostra strikes within seventy-two hours as intelligence suggests, a static defense means certain annihilation. Your plan leaves six thousand civilians, including the elderly, to die behind the lines because we refuse to move them. A fighting withdrawal tonight saves the brigade intact to defend Mirov later. We do not abandon soldiers; we save them from a slaughter. Building a hidden crossing ensures supply continuity. Negotiating now forces Vostra to hesitate. We act on facts: moving guns back buys time for evacuation without surrendering the political high ground. Let us preserve our force and our conscience by leaving tonight.

transcript.name: Robin Castell
transcript.speech: Quinn, you speak of conscience while planning an evacuation that leaves six thousand civilians behind. Is saving a unit worth abandoning our own people? You say intelligence predicts an attack, but I tell you the enemy fears us most here. If we pull back now, Vostra sees weakness and pours everything into Mirov tomorrow. We have one reserve brigade; let them defend Mirov while we hold this fortress. Our allies vote next week on aid. Do we lose their support because we ran from a hard fight? Hold the line tonight. Let our soldiers' courage prove that Kaldmark stands firm, not that it flees when supplies drop. Stay put.

transcript.name: Quinn Marlow
transcript.speech: Robin, your plan trades today's safety for tomorrow's slaughter. You fear losing allies' trust, but a dead brigade cannot defend Mirov or win future votes. Our nine-day ammunition clock does not lie; static defense invites an attack we cannot survive. A fighting withdrawal tonight saves the entire unit to reinforce Mirov and evacuate civilians before Vostra strikes. We negotiate a corridor and pull back artillery to force their hand, ensuring safe passage without surrendering the fortress's strategic value. This is the only way to preserve our soldiers, protect our people, and keep Kaldmark standing in the next aid vote.

transcript.name: Robin Castell
transcript.speech: Quinn asks us to trade our soldiers' lives for a slogan. You say we must run, but look at the civilians Quinn leaves behind. Six thousand people, including the elderly, cannot walk across a watched bridge while artillery shells rain down. Your plan abandons them to Vostra's mercy. Yes, ammunition is low. Yes, morale is brittle. But courage is not just surviving; it is standing firm when everyone else flees. If we withdraw now, Vostra takes Halden and marches on Mirov before our reserve can react. We hold tonight. We fight until allies arrive in three weeks. Then we move, taking our people with us. Do not give the enemy a victory built on our cowardice. Stand with Sergeant Kael. Defend the line.
